title: Boss: The Performance Pass
summary: A slow library dashboard: kill the N+1s, keep it to one query per widget, and page it properly.

steps.title: Make it fast
body: The library dashboard is slow. Each widget below works, but runs far too many queries. Rewrite each one so it returns the same result with a fixed, small number of commands. The tests count every command.
class Author { int Id; string Name; List<Book> Books; }
class Book   { int Id; string Title; int Year; int AuthorId; Author Author; List<Review> Reviews; List<Tag> Tags; }
class Review { int Id; int Stars; int BookId; }
class Tag    { int Id; string Name; List<Book> Books; }
Four books: Earthsea (Le Guin, 1968, 2 reviews), The Dispossessed (Le Guin, 1974, 1 review), Dune (Herbert, 1965, 3 reviews), Emma (Austen, 1815, no reviews).
Tags: Earthsea and Emma are `classic`; The Dispossessed and Dune are `classic` and `scifi`.

steps.title: The leaderboard
steps.prompt: `Leaderboard` lists authors by total review stars (highest first, then by name). It loads each author's books, then each book's reviews: an N+1 inside an N+1. Rewrite it to run **one** command.
template: new Author { Name = "Le Guin", Books = [new() { Title = "Earthsea", Year = 1968, Tags = [classic], Reviews = [new() { Stars = 5 }, new() { Stars = 4 }] },
new() { Title = "The Dispossessed", Year = 1974, Tags = [scifi, classic], Reviews = [new() { Stars = 5 }] }] },
new Author { Name = "Herbert", Books = [new() { Title = "Dune", Year = 1965, Tags = [scifi, classic], Reviews = [new() { Stars = 5 }, new() { Stars = 3 }, new() { Stars = 4 }] }] },
new Author { Name = "Austen", Books = [new() { Title = "Emma", Year = 1815, Tags = [classic] }] });
Dojo.Eq("the leaderboard", new List<string> { "Le Guin: 2 books, 3 reviews, 14 stars", "Herbert: 1 books, 3 reviews, 12 stars", "Austen: 1 books, 0 reviews, 0 stars" }, Leaderboard(dojoDb));
public Author Author { get; set; } = null!;
protected override void OnConfiguring(DbContextOptionsBuilder options) => options.UseSqlite("Data Source=library.db")

.LogTo((id, level) => id == RelationalEventId.CommandExecuted, e => { Commands++; LastSql = ((CommandExecutedEventData)e).Command.CommandText; if (Print) Console.WriteLine("SQL> " + LastSql.ReplaceLineEndings(" ")); });
hints: Project per author: `a.Books.Count`, `a.Books.SelectMany(b => b.Reviews).Count()` and `.Sum(r => r.Stars)`.
Sort in SQL on the projected numbers, then format after `AsEnumerable()`.

steps.title: The tag cloud
steps.prompt: Keep your leaderboard and add `List<string> TagCloud(LibraryDb db)`: each tag as `"classic (4)"`, most-used first, then by name, in **one** command. (The slow version would load every tag and then count each one's books with a separate query.)

steps.title: The shelf
steps.prompt: Add `(List<string> Titles, int? NextYear, int? NextId) Shelf(LibraryDb db, int size, int? afterYear, int? afterId)`: books oldest first (by `Year`, then `Id`), **keyset**-paged, read without tracking, one command per page. The cursor is the last book's `(Year, Id)` when there are more books, otherwise both are `null`.
starter: (List<string> Titles, int? NextYear, int? NextId) Shelf(LibraryDb db, int size, int? afterYear, int? afterId) => ([], null, null);
solution: (List<string> Titles, int? NextYear, int? NextId) Shelf(LibraryDb db, int size, int? afterYear, int? afterId)
if (afterYear is int y && afterId is int id)
query = query.Where(b => b.Year > y || (b.Year == y && b.Id > id));
return (page.Select(r => r.Title).ToList(), more ? page[^1].Year : null, more ? page[^1].Id : null);
